ai_summary: Great Britain is currently recording a total GB wind output of 8.7 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output reaching 3.3 GW, accounting for 32.7% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Thanks to this robust renewable dispatch, Scottish carbon intensity has dropped to 0 gCO2/kWh versus 74 gCO2/kWh GB-wide, underscoring the vital role Scotland plays in low-carbon generation. Nevertheless, severe transmission bottlenecks between Scotland and major demand centres to the south prevent the complete integration of this green electricity. Consequently, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 8,066 MWh at a constraint cost of about £212,472 through Balancing Mechanism bids. Because this clean power could not be transported to end-users, thermal generators had to compensate, resulting in an estimated 1,532,483 m3 of gas burned elsewhere and producing an additional 2,823 tonnes CO2. Annualizing these dispatch inefficiencies reveals an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £78 million. Since balancing charges are recovered directly from consumers, this constraint activity increases everybody's invoice in the UK by an estimated £0.30/MWh, demonstrating the dual environmental and financial penalty of grid infrastructure limitations.
